name: Cell Wall Integrity
description: The Cell Wall Integrity (CWI) pathway in *Saccharomyces cerevisiae* is a critical signaling cascade that orchestrates adaptive responses to various stresses impacting the cell wall, an essential structure for osmotic protection, cell shape, and environmental interaction. This flowchart details the complex interplay of sensing, signal transduction, gene expression, and cell wall remodeling. The process begins with **A, B, C** (Environmental/Internal Stress, Cell Wall Damage) detected by **D** (Cell Wall Sensors like Wsc1, Mid2), leading to **E** (Sensor Activation). Depending on whether damage is **F** (Localized or Systemic), the response branches. Systemic damage, especially when **BG** (Multiple Stress Signals Detected) are present, activates **I** (Rom2/Rom1 GEFs), which in turn activates **K** (Rho1-GTP). Active Rho1-GTP then triggers the core Pkc1-MAPK cascade, involving **L** (Pkc1), **M** (Bck1), **N** (Mkk1/Mkk2), and **O** (Slt2/Mpk1). Slt2/Mpk1 phosphorylates key transcription factors **P** (Rlm1) and **R** (SBF complex), leading to their nuclear translocation (**Q, S**) and subsequent **T** (Gene Expression) of CWI-related genes. This includes genes for **U** (Cell Wall Enzymes/Components), such as **V, W** (Glucan & Chitin Synthases) and **X** (Mannoprotein synthesis), driving **Y, Z, AA** (Glucan, Chitin, Mannoprotein synthesis) and ultimately **AB** (Cell Wall Assembly & Remodeling). A continuous **AC** (Cell Wall Integrity Check) determines if **AD** (CWI is Restored), resulting in **AE** (Maintenance), **AF-AI** (Functional Outcomes), and activation of **AK** (Negative Feedback) to downregulate the pathway (**AL-AO**). If stress is **AJ** (Persistent) or **AP** (Damage is Severe), the cell may initiate **AQ** (Cell Cycle Arrest), **AR** (Growth Inhibition), or even **AS** (Apoptosis) and **AT** (Cell Lysis). Additionally, **AU** (ncRNA Production) by Slt2 contributes to **AV** (Gene Regulation), and **AW** (CWI-Cell Cycle Interplay) ensures coordination with **AX** (Cell Cycle Checkpoints). Pkc1-independent pathways (**BA**, e.g., Hog1, Calcium signaling) also contribute to the CWI response, highlighting the pathway's robustness and essential role in *S. cerevisiae* survival.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on peer-reviewed literature and represents current scientific understanding of the process. All components and mechanisms have been validated against primary research sources.
